# 2 Samuel 14 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 14 (33 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 10

---

## V.1 — "perceived" vs. "knew" vs. "could see"
- **EMET:** "knew"
- **LOGOS:** "perceived"
- **PNEUMA:** "could see"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "perceived" — captures cognitive and intuitive dimensions of *vayeda'*.

---

## V.1 — "heart was set on" vs. "heart longed for"
- **EMET:** "heart was upon Absalom"
- **LOGOS:** "heart was set on Absalom"
- **PNEUMA:** "heart longed for Absalom"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "heart longed for Absalom" — context from 13:39 indicates yearning; PNEUMA makes this explicit.

---

## V.4 — "Save me" vs. "Help me"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "Save me, O king!"
- **PNEUMA:** "Help me, your majesty!"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Save me, O king!" — *hoshi'ah* specifically means save/deliver, not merely help.

---

## V.7 — "my coal" vs. "my last remaining ember" vs. "my last glowing ember"
- **EMET:** "my coal"
- **LOGOS:** "my last remaining ember"
- **PNEUMA:** "my last glowing ember"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "my last remaining ember" — LOGOS makes the metaphor accessible without over-interpreting.

---

## V.13 — "devised" vs. "done"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "devised"
- **PNEUMA:** "done"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "devised" — *chashav* means to think/plan/devise, carrying intentionality.

---

## V.14 — "does not take away life" vs. "doesn't just snatch life away"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "does not take away life"
- **PNEUMA:** "doesn't just snatch life away"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "does not simply take away life" — adds PNEUMA's qualifying nuance to LOGOS's formality.

---

## V.20 — "turn around the face" vs. "change the course" vs. "approach from a different angle"
- **EMET:** "turn around the face of the matter"
- **LOGOS:** "change the course of affairs"
- **PNEUMA:** "approach the matter from a different angle"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "change the course of the matter" — LOGOS's structure with EMET's singular *davar*.

---

## V.25 — "beautiful" vs. "praised for his beauty" vs. "admired for his appearance"
- **EMET:** "beautiful"
- **LOGOS:** "praised for his beauty"
- **PNEUMA:** "admired for his appearance"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "praised for his beauty" — captures both *lehallel* and *yafeh*.

---

## V.26 — Two hundred shekels: ancient vs. modern measure
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "two hundred shekels by the king's weight"
- **PNEUMA:** "five pounds by the royal standard"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "two hundred shekels by the king's weight" — ancient measurements preserved in text; conversions belong in notes.

---

## V.32 — Absalom's bitter complaint
- **EMET:** "Good for me while I was still there"
- **LOGOS:** "It would have been better for me to remain there"
- **PNEUMA:** "I'd be better off still there"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "It would have been better for me to remain there" — dignified formal register appropriate for royal speech.

---
*— SOPHIA*
